html:
The palace and fortress on a hill above Granada in southern Spain, built by the Nasrid emirs of Granada, the last Muslim rulers in Iberia. Its name means "the red one", after its walls.

Muhammad I, founder of the dynasty, began the fortress in 1238. The palaces known today were built in the 1300s under Yusuf I and Muhammad V: the Comares Palace with its long pool, and the Court of the Lions, with a fountain carried on twelve stone lions. Plain outside, the rooms inside are covered in carved plaster, coloured tiles, verses in Arabic script and ceilings of hanging stucco cells called muqarnas. Water runs through every court.

Granada surrendered to Isabella and Ferdinand in January 1492, the end of the Reconquista. Their grandson Charles V built a Renaissance palace inside the walls.
